html:
SMTO-SCH-0013 — This schedule can't be paused or resumed anymore

GUID: a1c3c32c-d953-49d5-a31d-b4d7752a2504
Slug: schedule-state-conflict
Domain: SCH · Subsystem: sch

What happened

  • Pause and Resume only work on a schedule that is still running or paused. This one has already been cancelled or has finished, so nothing about it was changed.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Reload the Schedules page and find this schedule. Check its status label and its Next run line. Someone else, another browser tab or the Agent may have cancelled it, or it may have finished its last run.
  2. If it shows Cancelled or Completed and No future run, it can't be resumed. Select New schedule and set up the timing you want. A cancelled or finished schedule stays in the list as a record only; new future runs need a new schedule.
  3. If it still shows Pause or Resume, use that button once on the reloaded page. The page you used earlier was out of date; the reloaded page shows the schedule's real state.

What success looks like

  • The schedule shows the state you wanted on the Schedules page, or your new schedule appears with the right Next run time.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO, along with the schedule's name. Don't keep pressing Pause or Resume on an old page; reload first.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Schedule update was refused because it asked to set status active or paused on a schedule whose current status is cancelled or completed.

What this means

  • Update requests active/paused status for a schedule whose current status is outside active/paused. Schedule configuration and temporal checks do not themselves launch deferred work. Existing event/request identities, captured authority and original execution receipts remain authoritative; diagnostic rendering does not poll time or mutate scheduling state.

Why this can happen

  • Update requests active/paused status for a schedule whose current status is outside active/paused.

How to diagnose it

  • Refresh its current lifecycle and history before choosing a new trigger.

How to fix it

  • Re-read the schedule (GET the event or refresh the Schedules page) and check its status; ScheduleManagementService.update only accepts status active/paused when the stored status is already active or paused. For a cancelled or completed schedule, create a new schedule with the intended next trigger instead of resubmitting the old ID.
  • Refresh current schedule state. Resume or pause only an active or paused schedule; create a new schedule for another next trigger.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • An eligible active/paused schedule uses its normal controls, or new future work gets a deliberate new schedule.

What not to do

  • Do not submit a stale identifier or revision after another actor changed the resource.

Technical notes

  • Schedule configuration and temporal checks do not themselves launch deferred work. Existing event/request identities, captured authority and original execution receipts remain authoritative; diagnostic rendering does not poll time or mutate scheduling state.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
